newsitem.title: USA: Prosecutor says photographer raped murdered model.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutor says photographer raped murdered model.

text.p: A photographer who allegedly murdered a model during a photo shoot, sexually tortured the woman before killing her to keep her from telling, the prosecutors said at his trial on Monday.
But the man's attorney claimed that he had photographs to show the two had consensual sex and that the woman was killed accidentally last November.

The two versions were presented during opening arguments in the trial of freelance photographer Charles Rathbun, charged with murdering former Raiders football cheerleader Linda Sobek. The charge included "special circumstances" which meant he could face the death penalty.

Deputy District Attorney Stephen Kay told the jury in his opening statement that Rathbun, who specialised in photo layouts of fast cars and models, "acted out his perverted fantasy for sexual purposes."
He said Rathbun, 38, made an appointment with Sobek, 27, ostensibly to do a photo shoot for a sports utility vehicle.
At the remote Angeles National Forest location, some 50 miles (80 km) north of Los Angeles, Rathbun tied the woman and raped her anally with a foreign object, the prosecutor said.
Rathbun then choked Sobek to prevent her telling the police and buried her body in a shallow grave, Kay said.
Defence attorney Mark Werksman claimed was killed during an accident with the vehicle and Rathbun panicked and buried her, he said.
Rathbun was arrested at his Hollywood apartment last Thanksgiving after an attempted suicide. He led police to Sobek's body two days later.
